newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyzstan mulls halt to antimony production.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyzstan mulls halt to antimony production.

text.p: Kyrgyzstan may stop production of antimony because of low world prices and depleted reserves, a senior metals official in the former Soviet republic said on Tuesday.
"At the end of April or the beginning of May the (Kadamzhai) enterprise might stop from a lack of raw materials," Dastan Sarygulov, head of state precious metals concern Kyrgyzaltyn, told reporters.
"With the fall in world prices for antimony to $2,100 a tonne from about $5,000 in 1995, the Kadamzhai plant lost about 1.3 million soms ($100,000) in 1996," he said.
Sarygulov said the republic had planned to produce about 7,600 tonnes of antimony this year, way below the Kadamzhai refinery's 17,000 tonnes per year capacity.
The plant has been largely dependent on concentrates from Russia's remote Yakutia region and neighbouring Tajikistan.
Sarygulov said the presence of cheap Chinese antimony on the world market was unlikely to diminish in the next few years.
